Houses or condos and townhomes in Sullivan Station?
Sullivan Station also had 123 condos and townhomes listed and 16 sold in October, against 79 houses listed. The Sullivan Station condos and townhomes page has those figures.

blocks.text: Sullivan Station Houses: streets and boundaries

items.t: The plan names the area's two commercial nodes: Panorama Heights at 152 Street and Highway 10, and Sullivan Heights at 64 Avenue and 144 Street — Sullivan Park at 6272 152 Street and Sullivan Elementary at 6016 152 Street sit on the 152 Street east edge.
Serpentine is a Fraser Valley Real Estate Board sub-area name in this part of Surrey; it is an MLS® area name, not a City of Surrey plan name — the City plan for these streets is South Newton.

blocks.text: Sullivan Station Houses: the housing stock

items.t: South Newton houses include a small-lot single-family pattern the City added on purpose: in December 2004 Council approved a single-family flex (small-lot) designation and guidelines in the South Newton NCP, on top of the plan's standard single-family and suburban half-acre and quarter-acre designations.

The current infill pattern is two-lot splits of suburban parcels: at 5744 146A Street a City report dated November 3, 2025 records a site zoned Suburban Residential Zone (R1), designated Suburban Residential Half-Acre, proposed for subdivision into two single-family lots under a Comprehensive Development (CD) zone based on R2.

blocks.text: Sullivan Station Houses: rules that affect buyers

items.t: The South Newton NCP no longer governs a purchase here. The City states South Newton was rescinded by the Surrey 2050 Official Community Plan (OCP) update and is no longer in effect, and that development in the area is now led by the OCP; on December 2, 2024 Council endorsed Corporate Report R246 updating land use designations to reflect current market conditions.

blocks.text: Sullivan Station Houses: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Sullivan Park is an 18.5-hectare (45-acre) community park at 6272 152 Street overlooking agricultural land east of Newton, with parking off 152 Street south of the train tracks or off 62A Avenue east of 152 Street — the rail line crosses the park's south access.

Sullivan Heights Park at 14426 64 Avenue is a 7.5-hectare park with soccer, rugby and cricket fields and a kabaddi field, and Sullivan Heights Secondary and the Bell Performing Arts Centre sit directly south of it at 6248 144 Street.

There is no Surrey Libraries branch and no City recreation centre inside Sullivan Station; the nearest branches listed by Surrey Libraries are Newton at 13795 70 Avenue and Strawberry Hill at 7399 122 Street.

blocks.text: Sullivan Station Houses: development and new projects

items.t: King George Boulevard BRT is the corridor project touching the west boundary: in October 2023 the Mayors' Council selected King George Boulevard from Surrey Centre to White Rock as one of the region's first three BRT corridors, and TransLink is advancing planning work, with alignment, designs, costs and timelines not yet determined at announcement.

Three bus routes frame the area, per TransLink timetables effective January 5, 2026: route 342 (Newton Exchange / Langley Centre) runs through the area via Highway 10, 152 Street, 60 Avenue, 142 Street, 57 Avenue, 144 Street and 72 Avenue; route 345 runs the length of 152 Street on the east edge; route 364 runs along 64 Avenue on the north edge.
There is no SkyTrain station in or directly serving Sullivan Station at present, and no library-branch transit hub inside the area — Newton Exchange, reached by the 342, is the transfer point.

blocks.text: Sullivan Station Houses: risks and due diligence

items.t: Check creek lots first: the City's South Newton page states the area contains several fish-bearing creeks, including the headwaters of Archibald Creek, Sullivan Heights Creek, and tributaries of Hyland Creek, and Surrey's streamside Development Permit Areas (DPAs) can require a permit before land alteration or clearing near a watercourse.

Sullivan Heights Creek is a fish-supporting stream through Sullivan Heights Park that connects to the Serpentine River, so a lot backing onto the park's natural area is also backing onto a protected watercourse corridor — confirm setbacks in COSMOS, the City of Surrey Mapping Online System, per address.

blocks.text: Sullivan Station home prices: what sold, November 2025 to October 2026

68 houses sold in Sullivan Station with a median price of $1,397,200 (the middle half sold between $1,249,500 and $1,551,250), taking a median of 36 days to sell at 97.0% of the last list price; 10% sold above list. They had a median $446 per square foot, a median year built of 2010 and a median lot of 3,815 square feet.

faq.q: How many houses are for sale in Sullivan Station?
faq.a: The Fraser Valley Real Estate Board counted 79 houses listed in Sullivan Station at the end of October 2026. The number changes daily, so ask Jared for today’s count.

faq.q: Is Sullivan Station a buyers’ or sellers’ market for houses?
faq.a: Sullivan Station houses sold at a sales ratio of 20% in October 2026, a balanced market on the reports’ scale (under 12% favours buyers, over 20% favours sellers).

faq.q: How many houses sold in Sullivan Station from June to October 2026?
faq.a: Between June and October 2026, 45 houses sold in Sullivan Station; Surrey as a whole recorded 464.

faq.q: Which secondary school serves a Sullivan Station house, and is it full?
faq.a: Sullivan Heights Secondary at 6248 144 Street is the local secondary, and it is over capacity. A City planning report dated November 3, 2025 states that, as of September 2025, Sullivan Heights was operating at 123 percent capacity despite a 700-capacity addition that opened in September 2022, with no further capital requests currently planned.

faq.q: Which elementary schools feed Sullivan Heights?
faq.a: Seven elementaries are in the Sullivan Heights family for 2026–2027: Cambridge, Goldstone Park, Hyland, McLeod Road Traditional, Snokomish, Sullivan and Woodward Hill. Note the name is McLeod Road Traditional, not McLeod Road Elementary, and catchment is still by exact address, so confirm the house in the district school locator.

faq.q: Can I split a large Sullivan lot into two house lots?
faq.a: Only with City approval, on the recent evidence. At 5669 146A Street a May 11, 2026 planning report sought subdivision into two residential lots, requiring an NCP amendment from Suburban Residential 1/2 Acre to Suburban Residential 1/4 Acre and rezoning from R1 to a CD zone based on R2 — budget for that process, not a simple subdivision.

faq.q: What did houses in Sullivan Station sell for?
faq.a: 68 houses sold in Sullivan Station from November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026, at a median price of $1,397,200.

faq.q: How long do houses take to sell in Sullivan Station?
faq.a: Half sold in 36 days or less, at a median 97.0% of the last list price; 10% went over asking (sales from November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026).
